title: Month Eight

source.title: 'A bunch of s**t': NC voters slam Trump's broken promise not to start new wars
source.hosts: Alex Tabet (reporter, on the ground in Fayetteville / Fort Bragg) · two Trump voters in the open (V1 a three-time Trump voter with a son in the service; V2 a supporter who 'thought it would be a month-long war') · Chad (a shop owner, Afghanistan and Iraq veteran, 2024 Trump voter) · an unnamed veteran · Reagan Juan (Army, five years; fourth-generation soldier; 2024 Trump voter 'for just one reason') · the holder, clipped twice
source.note: published 10-30 16:00 UTC; the 10-30 sweep (matched on 'midterm'). The second MS NOW cut from this sweep: the open of this clip was lifted into the Osborn segment (s9HVOeT3qKw) cut yesterday as A Spine, where V1 and V2 were scored from the lift; here they are scored on their own tape (the 0:41 and 1:16–1:27 lines) — the two reads overlap by two lines and the cut says so. Filed yesterday as sightings (see-msnow-1030-no-new-wars-clip), cut today because the 10-31 and 11-01 sweeps never reached GitHub and this is the strongest uncut tape on the live object. Roster lastCut was 10-31 (A Spine)

object.label: the next offensive against Iran — the force (PG01 §5, the war that made the crunch): read from the LI corner through Trump voters around Fort Bragg on the Friday before the vote, against the holder's own clipped promise. The holder is on the tape twice, constitutive: 'the wars we never get into' (0:26) and 'I was the first president in decades who started no new wars' (0:48). The tape's lowest line is a veteran's clock: 'first this war was promised to never happen, then … four weeks … a couple months — now we're in month eight' (3:22). No strike is dated on this tape; the force is read as its own length

zAxis.pos: the force relents — the war ends, the promise holds in its latest phrasing, and no new strike follows the vote
zAxis.neg: it does not — month eight, the promise's third rephrasing already passed, and the voters who cast it as their one reason say 'don't do it'

transformNote: the shadow is the holder's own voice, clipped: success measured 'by the wars we never get into'; 'the first president in decades who started no new wars'. Against it the tape puts a clock in a veteran's mouth — never happen → four weeks → a couple of months → month eight — and a vote re-read: 'don't do it'. This is the same shadow A Spine (10-31) scored from the lift and the Fox page (today, Win or Come Home) carries as the vice-president's 'not a forever war'; here it is the holder's own sentence, undated on the tape (the clips' dates are owed to the record). No strike, no deal, no price on this tape; 'destroying our economy' and 'taking a toll on the economy' are the only touches on the crunch

log.what: cut from the 10-30 sweep on its second day as the queue (no 10-31 or 11-01 sweep on GitHub at run time), transcript on disk from the Mac's 10-31 pull. The LI corner's read of the force as its own length, through the voters who cast on the promise, with the holder's own sentence on the tape twice. My calls: cutting a second MS NOW clip from the same sweep (a different day, the rule is per day; the sighting was filed yesterday 'not cut — one MS NOW per day'); scoring V1 and V2 again on their own tape although A Spine scored them from the lift (two lines overlap; both cuts say so); Chad and the unnamed veteran scored vacancy at zero rather than left out; Trump @O on both clips as the principal (declared +1.0) with the clips' dates left to the record. Reversible

split.note: one station, four chairs: the reporter at 10–22 (the setting, the question, the biographies); the voters who read the promise against the clock at 14–26 (V2's 'a month-long war', Juan's 'month eight', 'the sole reason'); the voters who read it as grief or as a vote at 40–50 ('a bunch of s**t', 'it hurts', 'don't do it'); and the one who declines to read it at all — Chad, 58, 'humble yourself amongst those appointed above you', the tape's peak and its one vacancy. Juan runs 20 · 14 · 46 · 50 · 42 — the lowest line on the tape and three of the five highest, inside ninety seconds: the README's specimen in a voter

scoreboard.zRule: every line carries a z, inferred where implied (Sailor 2026-10-13); inferred lines are marked zInferred with a zWhy

lines.quote: North Carolina — a tightly contested Senate race; the community surrounding Fort Bragg, the largest military base in the country
lines.note: the setting: the slate and the base in one sentence; files to slate01 (NC-Sen)
lines.zWhy: a setting is not a reading of the force; zero

lines.quote: we wanted to ask Trump voters how they feel about the president's promise not to start any new wars
lines.note: THE QUESTION — the shadow put as the object: the promise, to be read against month eight by the people who voted on it
lines.zWhy: a promise put to its voters as a question is one the chair reads as broken

lines.quote: we will measure our success not only by the battles we win but also by the wars we end and perhaps most importantly the wars we never get into
lines.note: constitutive — THE SHADOW in the holder's own voice (clip, undated on the tape): the force promised away before it happened. Not Dia-scored

lines.quote: it's a bunch of s**t; quit saying it's over — it's over
lines.note: THE TITLE OF THE CLIP — one word for the war; 'quit saying it's over' is the shadow refused by a supporter
lines.zWhy: a supporter who hears 'it's over' as a thing to quit saying reads the war as on

lines.quote: I was the first president in decades who started no new wars
lines.note: constitutive — the promise's second clip, past tense; the sentence A Spine (10-31) had only from a voter's mouth. Not Dia-scored

lines.quote: you voted for this man three times — and now potentially your son could be going to danger
lines.note: the chair's question frames the cost as the son; the record clause under it is the vote, three times
lines.zWhy: a son potentially going to danger is a war the chair reads as continuing

lines.quote: he's going over there and starting wars that is destroying our economy; we go to war, we bomb, then we leave — what are we doing?
lines.note: THE CHALLENGE: the promise contradicted by its own voter — 'starting wars' against 'no new wars' — with the force's pattern named (bomb, then leave) and the crunch touched once, unsized
lines.zWhy: a voter who names the pattern reads it repeating

lines.quote: the war on Iran is dragging on too long; I was supportive in the beginning when I thought it would be a month-long war
lines.note: the war's clock, dated by expectation — a month — against month eight; the object sized by its length
lines.zWhy: a month-long war in its eighth month is one not relenting

lines.quote: they said — I'm not going to start a war, I'm going to stop wars; he should keep his promise, no war
lines.note: THE PROMISE in the voter's mouth, as the object's own predicate (scored in A Spine's open from the lift; here on its own tape)
lines.zWhy: a promise a supporter asks him to keep is one the record shows broken

lines.quote: Fayetteville — an estimated 17% of the metro area is veterans; flags downtown
lines.note: the setting sized; files to slate01
lines.zWhy: a town's veteran share reads neither way; zero

lines.quote: Chad voted for Trump in 2024, served in Afghanistan and Iraq; acknowledges the war is taking a toll on the economy, but says it's part of the military culture not to question the commander-in-chief
lines.note: the toll granted and the reading declined, in the chair's report — the crunch from the LI corner, unsized
lines.zWhy: a toll acknowledged in month eight is a war still running

lines.quote: you learn how to humble yourself amongst those appointed above you; the moment you get on the side of naysaying them or become a shadow governor, you are discrediting what we're all supposed to be standing for
lines.note: THE PEAK — the one voice that declines to read the object; deference as the frame, 'shadow governor' the vehicle; vacancy
lines.zWhy: a reading refused reads neither way; zero

lines.quote: we have to be able to speak out; that's why I served in the first place
lines.note: the counter-frame to Chad's — speaking out as the service — still off the object; vacancy
lines.zWhy: the right to speak reads neither way on the force; zero

lines.quote: Reagan Juan served five years in the Army; a fourth-generation soldier; after the chaotic end to Afghanistan she voted for Trump in 2024 for just one reason
lines.note: the biography that sets up the tape's lowest line; the vote dated and its reason named
lines.zWhy: a vote cast on a promise about wars reads the wars as the test

lines.quote: his promise not to start any foreign wars — that was the sole reason
lines.note: THE PROMISE as the vote's single reason: the shadow and the ballot in one clause
lines.zWhy: a sole reason now being asked about is one the voter reads as failed

lines.quote: first this war was promised to never happen, then promised to be four weeks, a couple weeks, then a couple months — now we're in month eight
lines.note: THE CLOCK — the tape's lowest line: the promise's three rephrasings dated against the eighth month, in a veteran's mouth. THE TITLE
lines.zWhy: a promise rephrased three times and passed three times is a force not relenting

lines.quote: that's such a big promise — this is people's lives, our real lives; prolonging this war is both reckless and economically wasteful
lines.note: 'reckless' and 'wasteful' the vehicles; 'prolonging' the record clause; the crunch touched a third time, unsized
lines.zWhy: a war being prolonged is one not relenting

lines.quote: that promise obviously doesn't mean anything; it hurts when your words don't mean anything — it's so clear and blatant
lines.note: the shadow read as void by the voter who cast on it; 'it hurts' the vehicle
lines.zWhy: a promise read as meaning nothing is a war read as continuing

lines.quote: if you could go back to election day 2024 — don't do it; I didn't use my better judgment; I'm telling myself don't do it
lines.note: THE VOTE RE-READ — the closing line; the ballot withdrawn in hindsight
lines.zWhy: a vote withdrawn over the war is a war the voter expects to go on
